proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure); Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ, and Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i : Fin n) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ. For a linear map T : ℝⁿ → ℝ^k, JT := √det(⟨T e_i, T e_j⟩)_{i,j} (Gram-determinant Jacobian); for a map φ, Jφ(w) := J(fderiv ℝ φ w). For B ⊆ X, a map f and a weight h ≥ 0, the fibre sum is N_B(y) := Σ_{x ∈ B, f(x) = y} h(x), the unordered sum in [0,∞] (∑' over the subtype {x // x ∈ B ∧ f x = y}). c-antilipschitz on Ω means c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This is the linear algebra of step 3 of the parent proof (simpleNVector(A_w e) = det(B)·simpleNVector τ = ±det(B)·ξ(x), push forward by L(x)_#, take norms), stated for one linear map. The hypotheses (S1), (S2) are the two parts of the antecedent.

1. (Coefficients.) Put a_i := A e_i. Since a_i ∈ span(range τ), a_i = Σ_k c_k τ_k for some c (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun). Taking the inner product with τ_k and using orthonormality (⟨τ_k, τ_k⟩ = |τ_k|² = 1 and ⟨τ_k, τ_j⟩ = 0 for j ≠ k) gives c_k = ⟨τ_k, a_i⟩. Define the real n×n matrix B_ik := ⟨τ_k, a_i⟩; thus a_i = Σ_k B_ik τ_k for every i.
2. (Change of frame.) By (S2) applied to B and τ: simpleNVector a = det(B)·simpleNVector τ.
3. (Pushforward.) nVectorPushforward n L w = w ∘ covectorPullback n L is linear in w; in particular L_#(c·w) = c·L_#w and L_#(−w) = −L_#w (both hold by extensionality, definitionally). By nVectorPushforward_simple, L_#(simpleNVector a) = simpleNVector(L∘a). Hence, by step 2, simpleNVector(i ↦ L a_i) = det(B)·L_#(simpleNVector τ).
4. Since ξ = ±simpleNVector τ, L_#ξ = ±L_#(simpleNVector τ), so ‖L_#ξ‖ = ‖L_#(simpleNVector τ)‖ (norm_neg).
5. (Gram roots.) For any R and any family v : Fin n → ℝ^R, (S1) gives det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩) = ‖simpleNVector v‖², hence √det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩) = ‖simpleNVector v‖ (Real.sqrt_sq, norm ≥ 0).
6. (Unit frame.) τ orthonormal means ⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩ = δ_ij (orthonormal_iff_ite), so the Gram matrix of τ is the identity, with determinant 1; by (S1) ‖simpleNVector τ‖² = 1, so ‖simpleNVector τ‖ = 1.
7. (Scalars.) For c ∈ ℝ and an n-vector w, ‖c·w‖ = |c|·‖w‖ (operator norm; in Lean, if instance search does not provide NormSMulClass ℝ on NVector, prove ≤ by ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_smul_le and ≥ for c ≠ 0 by applying the same bound to c⁻¹·(c·w)).
8. (Conclusion.) Left side = ‖L_#ξ‖·‖simpleNVector a‖ (step 5 with R = P) = ‖L_#ξ‖·|det B|·‖simpleNVector τ‖ (steps 2, 7) = ‖L_#ξ‖·|det B| (step 6). Right side = ‖simpleNVector(i ↦ L a_i)‖ (step 5 with R = Q) = |det B|·‖L_#(simpleNVector τ)‖ (steps 3, 7) = |det B|·‖L_#ξ‖ (step 4). The two sides agree. (For n = 0 everything is uniform: B is the empty matrix, det B = 1.) ∎
key_steps: Expand A e_i = Σ_k B_ik τ_k with B_ik = ⟨τ_k, A e_i⟩ (orthonormality).
(S2): simpleNVector(A e) = det B · simpleNVector τ; push forward by L (nVectorPushforward_simple, linearity in w).
(S1): √det Gram(v) = ‖simpleNVector v‖, and ‖simpleNVector τ‖ = 1 for orthonormal τ.
